1) The synthesis and characterization of strapped porphirns and face-to-face dimers of porphirns were achieved by the condensation of 2,2′dipyrrylmthanes with dialdehydes in the presence of trifluoroacetic acid.

(i) strapped porphyrin was prepared directly by acid-catalyzerd condensation of 2,2′dipyrryl-methane with methyldioxy bridged dialdehyde, (ii) face-to-face dimesic porphyrin were obtained by condensation with dialdehydes having short chains, (iii) distortion of porphirin ring in short chain strapped porphyins was confirmed by their ¹H NMR data, red-shift

strapped porphyrin was prepared by the acid-cata-lyzed condensation of diethyl-dimethyl-dipyrrylmethanes with methylenedioxo-bridged dialdehydes having longer bridging carbon atoms than 5, and face-to-face dimers were obtained with shorter chains.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the synthesis of porphyrins with a methylene chain bridged between two pyrrole rings.
synthesis of strapped porphin and dimeric porphin.
the synthesis, structure, and spectroscopy of porphyrins with a variety of bridging groups.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

, in the case of the methylenedioxygen-bridged dialdehydes, the acid catalyzed condensation with the dipyrrylmethanes leads to strapped porphyrin products when the bridging carbon atom number is 5 or more, and to dimeric porphin products when it is less than 5.

strapped porphyrin can be synthesized by one-pot method and that the bridged carbon atom length between two porphyrin units is an important factor for the formation of strapped porphrins and face-to face dimmers.
the length of the bridging chain is an important factor for determining the structure of the product.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a face-to-face porphyrin dimer is formed in the presence of a short chain dialdehyde.

the acid-catalysed condensation of dipyrrylmethanes with dialdehydes is an effective method for the synthesis of strapped porhyrins, and the bridging carbon atoms should be longer than 5 to avoid the formation of dimeric porphyins.
strapped porphyrin synthesis is possible with longer chains and the face-to-face dipyrrylmethanes are possible with shorter chains.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the acid-catalysed condensation of 2,2′,6,6′-tetramethyl-3,3′,4,4′,5,5′-hexahydroxy dipyrrole with methylenedioxyl bridged dialdehyded affords strapped porphyrin.
the length of the methylenedioxygen bridging group plays an important role in determining the structure of the product.
it is possible to control the formation of face-to-face dimes by the length of the bridging chain and the reaction condition.
